---
name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Extract an evidence-backed backend dependency PRD from a delivered frontend, then build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify the matching Domainry source-owned application through one project-visible development TODO. The Skill keeps frontend evidence read-only while settling requirements and domain truth, authors declarative backend/model/*.json metadata, and records evidence-located frontend defects as findings for the frontend owner instead of repairing them. Use for frontend-to-Runtime replacement, new backend projects, existing-project increments, metadata-first backend implementation, Runtime integration, full-stack defect routing, and final verification.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Drive every development batch through:

```text
requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done
```

Platform capabilities determine the implementation mapping; they never determine the business facts. Do not start from Dataset, Report, metadata, an Action shape, or another Runtime feature and work backward into a domain model. Settle occurred facts, summaries, simulations, calculation ownership, persistence, and correction before capability discovery. Only two or more unresolved, mutually incompatible choices that change an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow form a product business ambiguity; block only the smallest affected modeling slice. Missing optional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms are not product blockers. Contract discovery and reversible technical defaults are not substitutes for business facts.

The frontend under `frontend/**` is evidence of product demand, not automatically a complete business specification. Inspect routes, screens, typed API contracts, Mock adapters, tests, roles, states, and copy read-only while settling requirements and domain truth; never promote Mock behavior into business truth. This Skill never creates, modifies, or deletes `frontend/**`. Route each mismatch to the owner proved by the explicit requirement, published Runtime contract, typed frontend API, Mock/tests, and real behavior. A frontend- or Mock-owned mismatch is a finding for owner `frontend`, never a backend workaround or frontend edit.

## Route exactly once

Choose one route before loading supporting resources. Do not combine the routes.

### Whole-project development

For every normal requirements, build, repair, integration, acceptance, or whole-project continuation batch, read [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) **completely before starting** and use it as the only execution workflow. It contains the authoritative TODO/Gate process, full normal-development CLI map, project boundaries, phase rules, required reference routing, Runtime acceptance, and terminal policy. Follow every applicable routed reference it requires. A full batch reads the whole guide; a light batch may omit only TODO sections under the guide's explicit light-batch rules, never guide loading or an applicable authority.

The routing map below is a reachability contract, not permission to read only selected guide sections:

| Moved entrypoint section / contract | Whole-project authority |
| --- | --- |
| workflow, routing, and batch scale | [whole-project workflow](references/development-guide.md#whole-project-workflow) |
| loaded Skill, CLI identity, and normal command surface | [CLI identity and canonical command map](references/development-guide.md#cli-identity-and-canonical-command-map) |
| complete TODO, Gate first-execution receipts, and session ownership | [session TODO and Gate receipts](references/development-guide.md#session-todo-and-gate-receipts) |
| project ownership and frontend finding routing | [project and frontend boundaries](references/development-guide.md#project-and-frontend-boundaries) |
| requirements extraction and critical ambiguity | [requirements to domain facts](references/development-guide.md#requirements-to-domain-facts) |
| domain truth, settlement, list Report, and technical prevention Gates | [domain truth design](references/development-guide.md#domain-truth-design) |
| capability reconciliation and metadata modeling | [model and capability mapping](references/development-guide.md#model-and-capability-mapping) |
| declarative authoring and the only release command | [model apply is the only release](references/development-guide.md#model-apply-is-the-only-release) |

| semantic journey binding and highest-risk canary | [semantic execution and canary](references/development-guide.md#semantic-execution-and-canary) |
| managed Runtime and exact-denominator acceptance | [Runtime and acceptance](references/development-guide.md#runtime-and-acceptance) |
| evidence ceiling and terminal states | [done terminal policy](references/development-guide.md#done-terminal-policy) |
| initial credential and acceptance-identity safety | [system seed login](references/development-guide.md#system-seed-login) |

### Explicit source-finalization continuation

Use this route only when the caller explicitly requests `source-finalization-continuation`, accepts and freezes upstream requirements/modeling, confirms the current source-finalization checkpoint remains valid, and limits scope exactly to:

```text
valid Actions project check → source finalize → module-focused Go test
```

Run the loaded Skill's resolver once with an explicit project-relative focused package:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --profile source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

Before resolving or resuming this continuation, prove the original Host/Agent turn has actually ended. An outer exec session reporting `Unknown process id`, missing its timing trailer, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence and must never trigger a concurrent Agent against the same session. The returned `continuation` envelope atomically owns this session's three-Gate TODO, synchronized Gate IDs, current checkpoint identity, and exact `run_recipes`. Execute those recipes in order and use no other workflow. Do **not** read `references/development-guide.md`, `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`, or any whole-project reference for this profile.

This route is caller authorization, never inferred from project state. Missing, stale, unsafe, or ambiguous session/checkpoint/CLI identity, a package outside the project, a missing focused package, or a conflicting/partial session TODO fails closed. Do not repair such a conflict by deleting or rewriting managed state. The compact route does not bypass the Host's complete loading of this `SKILL.md` and does not change whole-project behavior.

### Explicit Runtime process continuation

Use this compact route when the caller asks only to recover the already-packaged managed Runtime start/status boundary. Use the current Host session ID for this fresh compact continuation; do not create or reuse a whole-project TODO for that session. It does not require loading the whole-project guide, verification references, TODO template, verification authorities, or Gate runner source. Resolve the machine-owned profile once:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile runtime-process-continuation \
  --runtime-address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>
```

When the session has no TODO, Gate state, or Runtime profile, the resolver atomically creates its canonical two-Gate minimal TODO, synchronized state, and profile. It owns the fixed labels, `runtime_start` → `runtime_status` kinds, Gate IDs, exact argv, source/Runtime/cohort bindings, current packaged bundle, packaged CLI, numeric loopback address, and all pinned identities. The tool guarantees that the actual listener is the requested loopback and records its proof; the Agent adds no bind command or listener check. Stdout is only the compact envelope with the remaining `run_recipes`; execute them in order. Do not supply or author a TODO, label, marker, Gate ID, bundle, command argv, or identity binding yourself. Re-resolve after start to obtain only the status recipe when recovering from compaction. A partial session, non-profile-owned TODO, symlink, extra/reordered/forged Gate, changed address/package/source/CLI identity, stale state, terminal failure, or conflict fails closed without deleting or overwriting caller state; a terminal Gate never reopens.

## Loaded Skill and CLI identity

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact filesystem path of the `SKILL.md` loaded for this task. Every Builder command, resolver, Gate runner, template, and reference must come from that same root. The package has one executable: `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Never discover it through `PATH`, substitute another installed Skill's binary, call Domainry Plane directly, or invent a neighboring command.

For whole-project work, the guide requires the default resolver once at task start and binds `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Host session ID, TODO, compact resume packet, one-time authoring context, and package identity to its result. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. For the explicit continuation, the compact resolver call above supplies and validates the same package CLI identity without loading whole-project context.

## Universal safety and evidence invariants

- Treat Runtime-owned identifiers, hierarchy values, principal claims, cursors, and other canonical representations as opaque. Resolve them through the published typed client, `GET /identity/principal-context`, a formal seed/admin path, or a persisted Runtime result and carry them unchanged. Never construct, trim, pad, normalize, inject, or query Runtime-owned persistence to discover them. A missing formal source blocks the affected journey.
- Keep project-owned authoring in `backend/model/*.json`, referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`, project-owned backend source/tests, and the current session's `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md`. Never hand-edit generated source, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned `.domainry/**` delivery state. Never create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that ignores its generated capabilities.
- `model apply` is the only normal-development release command. Its reviewed `--product-surfaces` value is an integration boundary, never frontend mutation authorization. Repair reported model/input failures and run the same product command through a new round-specific Gate; never reopen a terminal Gate, split publication/materialization, or bypass destructive/evolution review.
- Every check, finalize, and focused-test command must run through its own Gate on its first real execution. The runner serializes each session/Gate across processes from state read through product execution and atomic receipt/state commit, and any passed or failed command receipt makes that Gate terminal. Never run the command directly first, rerun it, search historical receipts, or attach another command's receipt. After repair, add a new round-specific TODO Gate or use a genuinely new Host session. A receipt proves only its original Gate and current bound identities; changed bound content may make its evidence stale but never reopens that Gate.
- Before model authoring, bind every acceptance journey to its requirement, formal actor/session/principal, canonical context and identifiers, isolated setup, command/read surfaces, non-empty positive oracle, exact denied/conflict and unchanged-state oracle, durable effect, and dependencies. Do not create a second plan. Scope-sensitive journeys use same-record contrasts through real Runtime sessions; arbitrary errors, empty results, and residue from another case do not prove success. For unchanged/replay record hashes, use `runtimeRecordDurableSnapshot` (or copied-harness `durable_record_snapshot`), never the whole HTTP response body.
- After current source finalization and focused tests pass, run one highest-risk semantic canary across formal identity/context resolution → command → persisted effect → actor-visible read-back before broad Runtime integration. A canary failure blocks dependents and is repaired once at its owner; it never shrinks the frozen model or acceptance denominator.
- Never claim above current evidence. Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Completion requires the applicable evidence Gate, an empty finding inventory, the guide's terminal policy, and the TODO consistency check; unresolved product prerequisites are implementation/Foundation defects, not cosmetic limitations.

# Project development guide Drive every development batch with one visible project document: ```text /.domainry/development/.md ``` The complete frontend under `frontend/**` provides concrete demand evidence through routes, screens, typed APIs, Mock adapters, tests, states, and copy. It may omit business rules or encode provisional assumptions, so inspect it read-only while extracting requirements and domain truth. The CLI-compiled capability disclosure and Runtime machine contracts remain authoritative for data, authorization, navigation, and operation semantics. Frontend source and dependencies stay externally owned and read-only throughout the task; the recorded scope and evidence-based defect routing below turn frontend-owned defects into findings, never edits. See [backend-runtime.md](backend-runtime.md) for the closed backend Runtime boundary. The fixed stage order is: requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done. Requirements and domain facts always precede Runtime capability selection; platform shape never supplies business truth. ## Batch scale First record `Execution scope: requirements_only` or `implementation`. Use `requirements_only` only when the user requests analysis, requirements, or domain design and explicitly excludes development. It keeps the header, requirements, domain-truth design, and done sections; omit model, apply, Runtime, and verify sections with that reason in the header. Its `done` proves only the accepted requirements/domain artifact and must report no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim. Any build, repair, integration, or end-to-end request is `implementation` and follows the normal full/light rules below. Classify every batch as `full` or `light` and record the classification with its justification in the TODO header. A light batch is an existing-project increment with no new Object, Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change; everything else is a full batch. In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging. The caller-explicit `source-finalization-continuation` route is selected and initialized from the loaded entrypoint before any whole-project resource is read. It never loads this guide, the TODO template, or another whole-project reference; its compact Gate-owned envelope is its complete workflow. For every normal whole-project session, use the following initialization unchanged. At the start of an Agent session: 1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once. 2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`. 3. Resolve the session ID from the resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; the temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, borrow, or reuse another session's ID. 4. If `.domainry/development/.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session. 5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`. 6. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, scope, one `Frontend mutation scope`, and `requirements` as the initial current stage before implementation. 7. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan. 8. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; never check later work merely because it happened out of order. Close checkboxes through the evidence Gate's `run`, `attach`, or explicit `mark --status not_applicable` commands, not by writing success prose. Before leaving a stage, require `status --stage --require-complete`. Before any Host resume, first prove the original Agent turn has actually ended; an outer exec wrapper reporting `Unknown process id`, losing its timing output, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence. Never start a second Agent against the same session TODO/Gates while the first may still be alive. 9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes. For `requirements_only`, the formal Gate identity is the deterministic requirements-evidence closure exposed as `requirements`: the mandatory non-empty `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`; root `requirements.md` when it exists; and, when `frontend/src/**` contains a regular source file, the complete regular-file evidence under `frontend/**` after excluding dependency, build, coverage, cache, database, log, backup, and temporary artifacts. Paths and content hashes are sorted and framed, so creation order, timestamps, worktree location, backend files, unrelated root files, and derived frontend files do not affect the identity; symlinks fail closed. A frontend-led or immutable external-reference PRD is valid without root `requirements.md`: the PRD records its authority and immutable frontend snapshot/commit or external citation, and the local frontend closure is bound automatically when present. Do not silently place another mutable local authority elsewhere; make it the canonical root `requirements.md` or incorporate its accepted facts and immutable reference identity in the PRD. Do not guess `--bind source` when no project source exists. After obtaining the Gate ID from `list`, invoke the same Gate runner with `attach --gate-id --status passed --evidence-type source_artifact --evidence-path docs/backend-requirements-prd.md --bind requirements`, or execute an applicable validator once with `run --gate-id --bind requirements -- `. Missing or empty PRD makes the binding unavailable. The requirements-only terminal “all in-scope requirements” Gate uses this closure and does not demand an implementation-coverage receipt; a change to any included evidence makes it stale. Every validation argv must itself fail closed: use no pipeline, or place `set -o pipefail`/`set -euo pipefail` inside the executed shell script before any pipeline; `tee` never turns an internal failure into a passing Gate. One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document and owns only `.domainry/development/.md`; never overwrite or update another session's document. A new session creates a new file even for related work and may reference prior session TODOs only as read-only handoff context. The TODO is the only progress ledger. Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to this document, finish the reachable round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate binds the artifact and exact fact proved. Changed evidence content or a bound source, requirements artifact, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, identity, or receipt-named artifact makes the Gate stale and requires current evidence. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs. The lightweight TODO checker only detects document consistency; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system. Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first. ## Round discipline For every validation round: 1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage. 2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence. 3. Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repeat until no open finding remains. Stop early only when continuation is impossible, risks data loss or security, corrupts protected state, or invalidates the remaining results. A recoverable failure is not a reason to stop the round. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation. For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey blocked by that root cause, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner once, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator. ## Project and frontend boundaries The canonical project-owned authoring surfaces are: ```text backend/model/*.json declarative backend metadata inventory backend/reports/*.sql project-owned Report SQL referenced by model sql_file backend/ project-owned Go source and tests plus generated platform source .domainry/development/.md current session TODO .domainry/ CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence ``` Git owns project-source development, so normal editors, patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source. `.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination exception under `.domainry/**`, with each file owned only by its matching Host session. Never hand-edit generated source; frozen Project Contracts; Runtime manifests; materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts; audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state. Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set. Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header: - `integration_authorized`: the user requested a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the task to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms project ownership; - `backend_only`: the user explicitly limited work to backend; - `externally_owned`: another tool or owner delivered the frontend; - `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation. The scope records authorization context only and never changes this Skill's edit boundary: `frontend/**` remains read-only in every scope throughout the task. During integration compare the requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response before assigning ownership. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a compatibility adapter, raw HTTP, fabricated fallback, altered Mock, or weakened test. Record a frontend- or Mock-owned defect as a finding with owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, and contract basis. If it blocks a backend journey, mark that journey blocked without relabeling the defect as a platform gap. End-to-end acceptance here means backend end-to-end through real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior bound to the TODO and Gate source identity. Browser-layer UI verification is outside this Skill's acceptance scope. ## New and existing projects For a new project: - Before any project-mutating `domainry-cli` command, require the exact project root to be one initialized Git worktree. If the new root is not inside another worktree, run `git init --initial-branch=main ` once and verify `git -C rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals the exact root. Never retry mutations before this check, initialize an existing project without authorization, or create a nested repository inside another worktree. - Preserve the full requirement; do not silently reduce it to an MVP, demo, phase, or core subset. - Establish users, roles, goals, lifecycles, exceptional paths, and the complete operation inventory before modeling. - Apply industry business practices where they clarify the requested product without expanding its scope. - Before first backend publication, model local/test-only non-human acceptance identities, their formal login/session path, required Workforce profiles and assignments, departments/jobs/positions, business menu definitions, role-menu assignments, and the minimum real records for every acceptance journey. The implementer may add the minimum contrasting identities needed to prove same-record allow/deny, data-Scope, and requester isolation; these are acceptance fixtures, not evidence of the product's organization size or role cardinality. Do not defer these prerequisites to verify or seed online credentials. For an existing project: - Read current requirement documents, Git state, backend source, metadata, tests, and managed delivery state. - Record current behavior and the affected dependency closure in the TODO. - Plan only the requested increment and required regression coverage. - Retain valid existing source; do not rewrite it to manufacture workflow evidence. ## Initialization Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once at task start. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, session ID, TODO, compact `resume_packet`, one-time `authoring_context`, routed reference paths, and package identity to the result. `DOMAINRY_CLI` must equal the same package's single executable `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. Never resolve a CLI through `PATH`, substitute another Skill, or call Domainry Plane directly. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. These actions are setup rather than stages or TODO gates. Use only the applicable command families below, in TODO order. Add one pinned `--environment ` or `--service ` target wherever shown and keep it consistent. Use `--help` only to resolve listed-command flags; do not invent neighboring commands. The packaged CLI has no update, sync, doctor, audit, repair, rollback, migration, or generic contract-search surface. ```text # initialization "$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json # fixed capability discovery "$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-categories --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-category --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --key # complete declarative model, inspection, and one-time legacy bootstrap "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model preflight --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model validate --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" # the only release command; an existing delivery may require its emitted evolution review "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path --product-surfaces [target] [--allow-destructive] "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path --product-surfaces [target] --evolution-audit-sha256 --evolution-reason # approved source gaps "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" action context --projection coding --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 ] "$DOMAINRY_CLI" action scaffold apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 ] ... "$DOMAINRY_CLI" action source apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 ] ... --input - "$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector definition --json [target] "$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector context --projection coding --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector scaffold apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" ... # implementation-node evidence, then source closure # Gate-owned: run --cwd backend -- go test "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project check --json --scope actions --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" # verification, package, managed Runtime, and exact acceptance denominator "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project package --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" # With a fresh Host session ID, resolve the machine-owned Runtime Gate profile; it creates its own minimal TODO. "$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" --profile runtime-process-continuation --runtime-address 127.0.0.1: "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json "$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" ``` The only managed project-state root is `.domainry/builder/**`. Do not move, copy, merge, or recreate the managed root by hand. ## requirements ### Produce the backend dependency PRD For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. This is not a marketing PRD or a pixel inventory: it is the accepted demand contract for what Runtime and project metadata/source must provide. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline. **Reference mode for structured input.** A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as ` §N`. Then run `project acceptance check`. Every assertion obtains its session through `harness.session_for_case(case)`, uses `ScenarioGraph` for isolated setup/dependencies, and applies `ReasonOracle` for the declared status/error/state/audit/positive-control reason; never select a user from a role name, create profile headers, or read an internal identity table. The denominator is CLI-owned and never hand-edited. After a model evolution, run `project acceptance stale-report` and re-record only reported `stale`/`missing` cases, never the full set. Prose, arbitrary hashed text, or a coverage percentage cannot replace the harness. Record the whole verify round before repair. If any finding exists, return it to its model or implementation owner, repair the batch, and run verify again (Round discipline). ## done Record exactly one terminal state from [verification.md](verification.md): `done`, `acceptance_failed`, or `verification_blocked`, applying its failure classification and terminal policy. `done` requires every in-scope TODO item closed with concise current evidence, an empty finding inventory, a passing final verify round, every in-scope requirement mapped to implemented source and current validation evidence, and no requirement or limitation hidden, downgraded, or deferred. Product prerequisites such as identities, data, permissions, Runtime health, or persistence are implementation/Foundation defects, not environmental blockers. Do not claim `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done` above the highest evidence level reached; no structural pass upgrades delivery evidence into real-data behavior. For any terminal state, require the applicable `verify` and `done` Gate status, close every finding according to the terminal policy, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` immediately before the final response. Repair inconsistency and rerun until it passes. This linter pass is not test, Runtime, delivery, or scenario evidence. Provide a concise completion summary with implemented scope, test results, Runtime results, and explicitly non-blocking limitations. ## System seed login Runtime owns every initial credential. Never write credential rows, embed a password in model/source/TODO/evidence, or replace formal provisioning and password-change flows. A missing system/project seed credential is initialized from Runtime's deployment-owned `AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD`; production startup rejects the built-in development value and the credential is always marked `must_change_password:true`. A user created through the formal Identity API receives a cryptographically random per-user password exactly once in a `Cache-Control: no-store` response and must change it. Startup fills only a missing credential; it never overwrites an existing password hash, clears a lock, or undoes a changed password. The canonical system identity is user ID `admin`, login `admin@example.com`, Admin Console `/admin`, Surface `admin_console`. In a managed development Runtime started by this workflow, a deployment without `AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` seeds every missing credential — `admin` and project-declared acceptance identities — with development default `Domainry@2026`, marked `must_change_password:true`; production rejects this value. Establish a managed-development acceptance session by logging in with that default, completing forced change through `POST /auth/change-password` with `Idempotency-Key`, and keeping the new credential only in authorized secret handoff. Never print credentials into evidence or guess passwords: five failed logins produce `auth.account_locked`, and expiry does not lift the lock; an admin session must call `POST /identity/users/{userID}/unlock`. Formal Identity API users instead use their one-time no-store password. Business Workspace and Consumer Portal actors come from project-declared non-human acceptance identities. Authentication mode, session refresh, and authorization are independent of Surface; protected operations still enforce functional permission, ownership, Action policy, assurance, and data scope.

# Project development guide Drive every development batch with one visible project document: ```text /.domainry/development/.md ``` The complete frontend under `frontend/**` provides concrete demand evidence through routes, screens, typed APIs, Mock adapters, tests, states, and copy. It may omit business rules or encode provisional assumptions, so inspect it read-only while extracting requirements and domain truth. The CLI-compiled capability disclosure and Runtime machine contracts remain authoritative for data, authorization, navigation, and operation semantics. Frontend source and dependencies stay externally owned and read-only throughout the task; the recorded scope and evidence-based defect routing below turn frontend-owned defects into findings, never edits. See [backend-runtime.md](backend-runtime.md) for the closed backend Runtime boundary. The fixed stage order is: requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done. Requirements and domain facts always precede Runtime capability selection; platform shape never supplies business truth. ## Batch scale First record `Execution scope: requirements_only` or `implementation`. Use `requirements_only` only when the user requests analysis, requirements, or domain design and explicitly excludes development. It keeps the header, requirements, domain-truth design, and done sections; omit model, apply, Runtime, and verify sections with that reason in the header. Its `done` proves only the accepted requirements/domain artifact and must report no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim. Any build, repair, integration, or end-to-end request is `implementation` and follows the normal full/light rules below. Classify every batch as `full` or `light` and record the classification with its justification in the TODO header. A light batch is an existing-project increment with no new Object, Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change; everything else is a full batch. In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging. The caller-explicit `source-finalization-continuation` route is selected and initialized from the loaded entrypoint before any whole-project resource is read. It never loads this guide, the TODO template, or another whole-project reference; its compact Gate-owned envelope is its complete workflow. For every normal whole-project session, use the following initialization unchanged. At the start of an Agent session: 1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once. 2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`. 3. Resolve the session ID from the resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; the temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, borrow, or reuse another session's ID. 4. If `.domainry/development/.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session. 5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`. 6. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, scope, one `Frontend mutation scope`, and `requirements` as the initial current stage before implementation. 7. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan. 8. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; never check later work merely because it happened out of order. Close checkboxes through the evidence Gate's `run`, `attach`, or explicit `mark --status not_applicable` commands, not by writing success prose. Before leaving a stage, require `status --stage --require-complete`. Before any Host resume, first prove the original Agent turn has actually ended; an outer exec wrapper reporting `Unknown process id`, losing its timing output, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence. Never start a second Agent against the same session TODO/Gates while the first may still be alive. 9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes. For `requirements_only`, the formal Gate identity is the deterministic requirements-evidence closure exposed as `requirements`: the mandatory non-empty `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`; root `requirements.md` when it exists; and, when `frontend/src/**` contains a regular source file, the complete regular-file evidence under `frontend/**` after excluding dependency, build, coverage, cache, database, log, backup, and temporary artifacts. Paths and content hashes are sorted and framed, so creation order, timestamps, worktree location, backend files, unrelated root files, and derived frontend files do not affect the identity; symlinks fail closed. A frontend-led or immutable external-reference PRD is valid without root `requirements.md`: the PRD records its authority and immutable frontend snapshot/commit or external citation, and the local frontend closure is bound automatically when present. Do not silently place another mutable local authority elsewhere; make it the canonical root `requirements.md` or incorporate its accepted facts and immutable reference identity in the PRD. Do not guess `--bind source` when no project source exists. After obtaining the Gate ID from `list`, invoke the same Gate runner with `attach --gate-id --status passed --evidence-type source_artifact --evidence-path docs/backend-requirements-prd.md --bind requirements`, or execute an applicable validator once with `run --gate-id --bind requirements -- `. Missing or empty PRD makes the binding unavailable. The requirements-only terminal “all in-scope requirements” Gate uses this closure and does not demand an implementation-coverage receipt; a change to any included evidence makes it stale. Every validation argv must itself fail closed: use no pipeline, or place `set -o pipefail`/`set -euo pipefail` inside the executed shell script before any pipeline; `tee` never turns an internal failure into a passing Gate. One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document and owns only `.domainry/development/.md`; never overwrite or update another session's document. A new session creates a new file even for related work and may reference prior session TODOs only as read-only handoff context. The TODO is the only progress ledger. Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to this document, finish the reachable round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate binds the artifact and exact fact proved. Changed evidence content or a bound source, requirements artifact, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, identity, or receipt-named artifact makes the Gate stale and requires current evidence. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs. The lightweight TODO checker only detects document consistency; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system. Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first. ## Round discipline For every validation round: 1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage. 2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence. 3. Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repeat until no open finding remains. Stop early only when continuation is impossible, risks data loss or security, corrupts protected state, or invalidates the remaining results. A recoverable failure is not a reason to stop the round. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation. For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey blocked by that root cause, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner once, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator. ## Project and frontend boundaries The canonical project-owned authoring surfaces are: ```text backend/model/*.json declarative backend metadata inventory backend/reports/*.sql project-owned Report SQL referenced by model sql_file backend/ project-owned Go source and tests plus generated platform source .domainry/development/.md current session TODO .domainry/ CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence ``` Git owns project-source development, so normal editors, patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source. `.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination exception under `.domainry/**`, with each file owned only by its matching Host session. Never hand-edit generated source; frozen Project Contracts; Runtime manifests; materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts; audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state. Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set. Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header: - `integration_authorized`: the user requested a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the task to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms project ownership; - `backend_only`: the user explicitly limited work to backend; - `externally_owned`: another tool or owner delivered the frontend; - `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation. The scope records authorization context only and never changes this Skill's edit boundary: `frontend/**` remains read-only in every scope throughout the task. During integration compare the requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response before assigning ownership. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a compatibility adapter, raw HTTP, fabricated fallback, altered Mock, or weakened test. Record a frontend- or Mock-owned defect as a finding with owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, and contract basis. If it blocks a backend journey, mark that journey blocked without relabeling the defect as a platform gap. End-to-end acceptance here means backend end-to-end through real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior bound to the TODO and Gate source identity. Browser-layer UI verification is outside this Skill's acceptance scope. ## New and existing projects For a new project: - Before any project-mutating `domainry-cli` command, require the exact project root to be one initialized Git worktree. If the new root is not inside another worktree, run `git init --initial-branch=main ` once and verify `git -C rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals the exact root. Never retry mutations before this check, initialize an existing project without authorization, or create a nested repository inside another worktree. - Preserve the full requirement; do not silently reduce it to an MVP, demo, phase, or core subset. - Establish users, roles, goals, lifecycles, exceptional paths, and the complete operation inventory before modeling. - Apply industry business practices where they clarify the requested product without expanding its scope. - Before first backend publication, model local/test-only non-human acceptance identities, their formal login/session path, required Workforce profiles and assignments, departments/jobs/positions, business menu definitions, role-menu assignments, and the minimum real records for every acceptance journey. The implementer may add the minimum contrasting identities needed to prove same-record allow/deny, data-Scope, and requester isolation; these are acceptance fixtures, not evidence of the product's organization size or role cardinality. Do not defer these prerequisites to verify or seed online credentials. For an existing project: - Read current requirement documents, Git state, backend source, metadata, tests, and managed delivery state. - Record current behavior and the affected dependency closure in the TODO. - Plan only the requested increment and required regression coverage. - Retain valid existing source; do not rewrite it to manufacture workflow evidence. ## Initialization Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once at task start. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, session ID, TODO, compact `resume_packet`, one-time `authoring_context`, routed reference paths, and package identity to the result. `DOMAINRY_CLI` must equal the same package's single executable `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. Never resolve a CLI through `PATH`, substitute another Skill, or call Domainry Plane directly. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. These actions are setup rather than stages or TODO gates. Use only the applicable command families below, in TODO order. Add one pinned `--environment ` or `--service ` target wherever shown and keep it consistent. Use `--help` only to resolve listed-command flags; do not invent neighboring commands. The packaged CLI has no update, sync, doctor, audit, repair, rollback, migration, or generic contract-search surface. ```text # initialization "$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json # fixed capability discovery "$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-categories --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-category --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --key # complete declarative model, inspection, and one-time legacy bootstrap "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model preflight --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model validate --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" # the only release command; an existing delivery may require its emitted evolution review "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path --product-surfaces [target] [--allow-destructive] "$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path --product-surfaces [target] --evolution-audit-sha256 --evolution-reason # approved source gaps

Do not move, copy, merge, or recreate the managed root by hand. ## requirements ### Produce the backend dependency PRD For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. This is not a marketing PRD or a pixel inventory: it is the accepted demand contract for what Runtime and project metadata/source must provide. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline. **Reference mode for structured input.** A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as ` §N`. Test per requirement: if one section states the rule completely, cite it — do not restate it; rewrite only what must be assembled from scattered evidence (Mock adapters, tests, verbal decisions, multiple documents). A reference-mode PRD carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section; restating an already-structured source is prohibited waste. Both modes keep the Resolve-critical-ambiguity table and full traceability. Read frontend evidence in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/fixtures; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Legacy APIs or prior backends are `legacy_reference` until the current requirement or frontend confirms them. This inspection is read-only even when later integration is authorized to repair frontend source. A Mock fixture, adapter behavior, test expectation, or visible affordance proves demand or a current assumption; it does not establish a business rule without higher-precedence evidence. Use this precedence when evidence conflicts: 1. explicit current user decision; 2. latest accepted requirement or design contract; 3. latest implemented frontend behavior; 4. typed API and Mock semantics; 5. frontend tests; 6. legacy/reference implementation. Do not erase conflicts using precedence alone. Record the conflict, affected requirement IDs, selected authority, and confirmation evidence. Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract at least: - pages, routes, entry conditions, actors, journeys, and observable success; - canonical object identities, fields, relations, list/detail/form/report shapes, filters, search, sort, and pagination; - commands, outcomes, bulk operations, state transitions, approvals, cancellation/correction paths, and durable side effects; - roles, permissions, record scope, sensitive fields, menu visibility, and allow/deny behavior; - observable validation, conflict, retry, and replay behavior; discover Runtime-owned stable error categories/codes and choose concurrency/idempotency mechanisms after the business invariant is settled; - calculations with inputs, units, formula, policy/version date, rounding point/mode, examples, and refund/correction behavior; - schedulers, automations, notifications, connectors, files, audit, outbox, and external effects; - presentation-only behavior that remains `frontend_only` and must not create backend metadata. Build a traceability matrix with one row per requirement: `frontend evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Where the frontend exposes a typed API, count its backend-bound operations and account for every one in the matrix as implemented, platform-reused, frontend-only, superseded, or open. Every route must map to a journey or an explicit frontend-only disposition. Every write operation must name authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof; Runtime-owned codes and mechanism details may point to their contract-discovery or implementation-decision row. Matrix and contract-table cells are phrases, not sentences. Once a fact is in a table (or cited by section), do not restate it in prose; prose is only for what no table column captures. ### Resolve critical ambiguity Classify every unresolved choice in the PRD before capability selection. This is the authoritative requirements-only routing rule. An item is a `business_blocker` only when accepted evidence leaves at least two concrete, mutually incompatible choices and choosing among them changes a requirement's explicitly demanded observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow. A missing optional field, metadata value, preference, or mechanism is not a blocker when one deterministic conservative fallback preserves the stated core behavior. Apply the blocker only to the smallest affected requirement/model slice; never block an entire Object, Report, export, or Workflow because one optional field or later preference is open. | Decision class | Boundary | Required handling | Blocks model? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `business_blocker` | Two or more concrete, mutually incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the incompatible choices and the exact affected requirement/model items. Do not infer the choice from UI, fixtures, labels, legacy behavior, or implementation convenience; obtain a current user decision or accepted requirement evidence. | Yes, only for the smallest affected slice. | | `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal error code/category, canonical identifier or principal/context source, or the mapping of accepted facts to Action, Workflow, metadata, or another published capability | Discover it through the typed client, fixed capability categories, or another formal Runtime contract. If the formal contract is absent, record a Foundation/Runtime owner gap; do not turn it into a product question or invent a representation. | No. It may block affected implementation or acceptance after discovery fails, but not settled business modeling. | | `safe_implementation_decision` | A purely technical, reversible choice that preserves the accepted business invariant, including stable ordering with a unique tie-breaker, pagination maximum, index, internal resource key, and audit, idempotency, or concurrency mechanism | Use the published platform standard; otherwise record one deterministic, conservative safe default with its rationale and evolution path. | No. | | `product_follow_up` | A product preference whose currently documented fallback does not change required observable results, permission, amount meaning, or business state in the accepted scope | Record the assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger. Never relabel it `confirmed`. | No. | Security and privacy omissions use a conservative `safe_implementation_decision`: least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export by default, with the evolvable assumption recorded. If an explicit requirement demands export or broader disclosure of a sensitive fact, that conflict is a `business_blocker` until its authorization and disclosure boundary is confirmed. Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules: - If exact decimal representation, a comparison threshold, or summation is explicit, absent currency, unit, or numeric range metadata does not block the decimal field, comparison, or aggregation. Keep optional metadata nullable and enforce only stated command preconditions. Block only the smallest comparison/conversion slice when two incompatible units are actually possible and the required result depends on choosing or converting between them. - If an asynchronous approval task and its approved/rejected outcomes are explicit but the host lifecycle has no pending state, put pending state on an independent approval Object and leave the host unchanged until the terminal effect. Missing edit/cancel/resubmit behavior is a `product_follow_up`; use conservative concurrency/idempotency that grants no extra authority and produces no duplicate effect. - If a resource is explicitly non-updatable/non-deletable but no business-role read is required, model the resource and immutable deny rules without inventing a read actor. Prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence; do not fabricate business read permission for acceptance. - If weekday/morning scheduling intent is explicit but timezone or holiday-calendar preference is absent, use the platform/deployment-configured deterministic timezone and a standard weekday cron, then record the preference as `product_follow_up`. Block only when the requirement explicitly demands different multi-timezone or statutory-holiday outcomes and choosing the calendar changes that required result. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring. Unspecified additional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms do not block already settled core behavior. A contract-discovery item or safe implementation decision can still fail its later implementation, security, or acceptance Gate; the classification changes who decides the fact, never the required proof or quality bar. ## domain truth design Read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) completely. Freeze the domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement; close every calculation's ownership/persistence/correction decisions per that document. A capability is an implementation option after these facts exist; it is not evidence for choosing them. Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts must remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, model the write-side atomic Action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its Reports. Keep every affected model item blocked until this Gate closes. ### Mandatory list Report and export Gate Before discovering or selecting a Report capability, settle its observable product invariants and record the applicable technical contracts below. An unresolved business result, permission, amount meaning, or state remains a `business_blocker`; unspecified reversible mechanics use the requirements decision routing above and do not become product questions. Extract at least: - pages, routes, entry conditions, actors, journeys, and observable success; - canonical object identities, fields, relations, list/detail/form/report shapes, filters, search, sort, and pagination; - commands, outcomes, bulk operations, state transitions, approvals, cancellation/correction paths, and durable side effects; - roles, permissions, record scope, sensitive fields, menu visibility, and allow/deny behavior; - observable validation, conflict, retry, and replay behavior; discover Runtime-owned stable error categories/codes and choose concurrency/idempotency mechanisms after the business invariant is settled; - calculations with inputs, units, formula, policy/version date, rounding point/mode, examples, and refund/correction behavior;

- schedulers, automations, notifications, connectors, files, audit, outbox, and external effects; - presentation-only behavior that remains `frontend_only` and must not create backend metadata. Build a traceability matrix with one row per requirement: `frontend evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Where the frontend exposes a typed API, count its backend-bound operations and account for every one in the matrix as implemented, platform-reused, frontend-only, superseded, or open. Every route must map to a journey or an explicit frontend-only disposition. Every write operation must name authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof; Runtime-owned codes and mechanism details may point to their contract-discovery or implementation-decision row. Matrix and contract-table cells are phrases, not sentences. Once a fact is in a table (or cited by section), do not restate it in prose; prose is only for what no table column captures. ### Resolve critical ambiguity Classify every unresolved choice in the PRD before capability selection. This is the authoritative requirements-only routing rule. An item is a `business_blocker` only when accepted evidence leaves at least two concrete, mutually incompatible choices and choosing among them changes a requirement's explicitly demanded observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow. A missing optional field, metadata value, preference, or mechanism is not a blocker when one deterministic conservative fallback preserves the stated core behavior. Apply the blocker only to the smallest affected requirement/model slice; never block an entire Object, Report, export, or Workflow because one optional field or later preference is open. | Decision class | Boundary | Required handling | Blocks model? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `business_blocker` | Two or more concrete, mutually incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the incompatible choices and the exact affected requirement/model items. Do not infer the choice from UI, fixtures, labels, legacy behavior, or implementation convenience; obtain a current user decision or accepted requirement evidence. | Yes, only for the smallest affected slice. | | `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal error code/category, canonical identifier or principal/context source, or the mapping of accepted facts to Action, Workflow, metadata, or another published capability | Discover it through the typed client, fixed capability categories, or another formal Runtime contract. If the formal contract is absent, record a Foundation/Runtime owner gap; do not turn it into a product question or invent a representation. | No. It may block affected implementation or acceptance after discovery fails, but not settled business modeling. | | `safe_implementation_decision` | A purely technical, reversible choice that preserves the accepted business invariant, including stable ordering with a unique tie-breaker, pagination maximum, index, internal resource key, and audit, idempotency, or concurrency mechanism | Use the published platform standard; otherwise record one deterministic, conservative safe default with its rationale and evolution path. | No. | | `product_follow_up` | A product preference whose currently documented fallback does not change required observable results, permission, amount meaning, or business state in the accepted scope | Record the assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger. Never relabel it `confirmed`. | No. | Security and privacy omissions use a conservative `safe_implementation_decision`: least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export by default, with the evolvable assumption recorded. If an explicit requirement demands export or broader disclosure of a sensitive fact, that conflict is a `business_blocker` until its authorization and disclosure boundary is confirmed. Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules: - If exact decimal representation, a comparison threshold, or summation is explicit, absent currency, unit, or numeric range metadata does not block the decimal field, comparison, or aggregation. Keep optional metadata nullable and enforce only stated command preconditions. Block only the smallest comparison/conversion slice when two incompatible units are actually possible and the required result depends on choosing or converting between them. - If an asynchronous approval task and its approved/rejected outcomes are explicit but the host lifecycle has no pending state, put pending state on an independent approval Object and leave the host unchanged until the terminal effect. Missing edit/cancel/resubmit behavior is a `product_follow_up`; use conservative concurrency/idempotency that grants no extra authority and produces no duplicate effect. - If a resource is explicitly non-updatable/non-deletable but no business-role read is required, model the resource and immutable deny rules without inventing a read actor. Prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence; do not fabricate business read permission for acceptance. - If weekday/morning scheduling intent is explicit but timezone or holiday-calendar preference is absent, use the platform/deployment-configured deterministic timezone and a standard weekday cron, then record the preference as `product_follow_up`. Block only when the requirement explicitly demands different multi-timezone or statutory-holiday outcomes and choosing the calendar changes that required result. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring. Unspecified additional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms do not block already settled core behavior. A contract-discovery item or safe implementation decision can still fail its later implementation, security, or acceptance Gate; the classification changes who decides the fact, never the required proof or quality bar. ## domain truth design Read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) completely. Freeze the domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement; close every calculation's ownership/persistence/correction decisions per that document. A capability is an implementation option after these facts exist; it is not evidence for choosing them. Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts must remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, model the write-side atomic Action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its Reports. Keep every affected model item blocked until this Gate closes. ### Mandatory list Report and export Gate Before discovering or selecting a Report capability, settle its observable product invariants and record the applicable technical contracts below. An unresolved business result, permission, amount meaning, or state remains a `business_blocker`; unspecified reversible mechanics use the requirements decision routing above and do not become product questions. Delivery and acceptance must still prove every applicable contract: 1. **List Report pagination:** every list Report has bounded server pagination: platform standard or `page_size` plus opaque cursor, maximum page size from the platform contract or a recorded safe default of 200, stable ordering with a deterministic unique cursor tie-breaker, explicit `truncated`, and `total_semantics` of `exact` or `at_least`. Page maximum and tie-breaker are `safe_implementation_decision` items when they do not change an accepted business ordering rule. A transport page that materializes the complete result before slicing is not bounded execution. 2. **Same-Report threshold routing:** export prepare makes one bounded probe of the same Report under normalized parameters and current authorization/data Scope. The fixed threshold is 1000: an exhausted `0..1000` probe yields the exact total and one synchronous governed CSV; observing row 1001 immediately routes to the platform asynchronous paged export-job substrate, whose terminal result records the final exact total. Both branches use the identical Report/SQL/source hash/parameters/Scope; no count-only or export-only second query is allowed. 3. **Asynchronous reauthorization and terminal notification:** before asynchronous page one, the worker reconstructs the current persisted project user-role principal in the frozen workspace and compares canonical authorization Scope, failing closed on real drift. It never substitutes a manifest-only role or synthetic Surface. Only this branch publishes requester-only `completed`/`failed` Inbox notifications linked through export job, audit, and artifact. 4. **Atomic fingerprint replay:** the server canonicalizes Report key, normalized parameters, SQL/source hash, requester/workspace, authorization/data-Scope hash, format, and result version. Equivalent requests atomically reuse an accepted/running job or a completed unexpired artifact without a second file, download record, or terminal notification. `audit_id` stays out of the fingerprint; only failed/cancelled work or expired/corrupt artifacts may create one new execution through database compare-and-create.
